steps.name: Pin DR-0009: a rebuild derives the seen-counters from the whole cache
criteria: A rebuild over a month-sharded cache holding the same job advertised in two different months reports Times Seen 2, not 1.
That rebuild reports First Seen as the EARLIER of the two sighting dates, so First Seen cannot drift forward.
The test is demonstrably non-vacuous: narrowing the derivation to a single shard makes it fail, and that failure is shown rather than asserted.
The test depends on no personal data — temp directories only, never .cache/.
All existing tests stay green: suite 110 passed / 7 failed / 1 skipped becomes 111 passed / 7 failed / 1 skipped.
steps.scenario_name: a rebuild derives the seen-counters from every shard, not one window
steps.implementation_notes: Pins the invariant recorded in DR-0009 (build derives from the whole cache). The hazard: First Seen, Last Seen and Times Seen are computed solely from the messages handed to one harvest() call (src/core/harvest.mjs:73-78 sets timesSeen: 1 for any job not already in that batch), and DR-0004 (every column has exactly one owner) makes harvester-owned columns always overwritten — so a window-scoped derivation writes the worse value over the better one, silently. Measured on the live corpus: IT Product Delivery Manager at Biffa reads First Seen 2026-09-08 / Times Seen 4 from a whole-cache rebuild, but First Seen 2026-09-09 / Times Seen 2 from a later-window harvest merged in. THIS TEST WILL BE GREEN ON ARRIVAL because the invariant currently holds — the --in rebuild reads the whole cache recursively since fix-reparse-silent-zero step 01-02 (d122bd3). A guard that cannot fail is not a guard, so non-vacuity must be DEMONSTRATED, not claimed: run the same assertions against a single shard and show them failing. The build subcommand is still a RED scaffold (src/cli/harvest.mjs:26), so --in is the only derivation path that exists to pin today; when build lands it must satisfy the same test.
